newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester says float plans go on.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester says float plans go on.

text.p: British building society Alliance & Leicester is proceeding with its plans for a stock market float although it is aware of proposals in a new Building Societies Bill which could affect the move, a spokesman said.
"At the moment we are steaming ahead, we are on schedule," he said on Thursday. "But we have cognisance the timing could be affected by the proposals," he added.

A report in Thursday's edition of the Times newspaper said the building society was considering abandoning the flotation after it had been advised its transfer document contained information that would be misleading under the planned Bill.
It said the plans could be abandoned after a board meeting of the building society on Thursday, but the spokesman said no further developments were expected during the day.
The planned flotation, estimated to be worth 2.5 billion stg, is due to be voted on by members of the society at a special meeting on December 10.
New legislation being drafted has abandoned a clause which gives converting societies five years protection from hostile takeover bids.
When the Alliance & Leicester drew up its transfer document, it was based on present legislation.
